Source.Title: Panchroma™ CoPE Technical Data Sheet
Source.Source note: Polymaker's six-page data sheet for Panchroma CoPE, version 5.4, as the Internet Archive captured it on 2025-11-04 12:49:41 UTC: physical, thermal and mechanical tables (the mechanical one in a classic and a high printing speed column), recommended printing conditions and how its test bars were made. The maker's address (https://polymaker.com/wp-content/uploads/lana-downloads/Panchroma-CoPE_TDS_EN_V5.4.pdf) answers 404; R-POLYMAKER-COPE-TDS-V5-4 recorded it not retrieved on 2026-09-13.
Source.Access note: Fetched 2026-10-07 by Claude Sonnet (quality round 2026-10-07, b45) as the raw capture (id_) of https://polymaker.com/wp-content/uploads/lana-downloads/Panchroma-CoPE_TDS_EN_V5.4.pdf, captured 2025-11-04 12:49:41 UTC; the document hashed is the file as the Internet Archive replays it. Staged by digest (ingest:witness --from). The maker does not serve it now.

Skipped: Melting temperature: prints N/A
Bending modulus (Z), both columns: N/A
Bending strength (Z), both columns: N/A
Notched Charpy impact strength (Z), both columns: N/A
MAX VOLUMETRIC SPEED table (p. 3): a printing-speed/flow table, not a profile
SURFACE GLOSSINESS table (p. 3, GU values by speed and temperature): a gloss table, not a profile

Page 5 HOW TO MAKE SPECIMENS settings (230 °C, bed 50 °C, shell 2, top & bottom 3, infill 100 %, ambient, fan ON): recorded in params of the mechanical values; it differs from the column footnotes (210 °C / 230 °C), a conflict inside the sheet
Page 5 specimen drawings (tensile, flexural, impact with 45° notch, Z axis arrows): no numbers recorded beyond the notch angle being in the drawing
Page 4 FAQ (do not print with PLA, glue caution, bed 40-50℃ not above 60℃, textured PEI not recommended): bed items kept in the profile notes only
Page 1 cover and page 6 disclaimer: no values
Environmental temperature "Ambient temperature" (p. 5): a specimen condition, not an enclosure recommendation

Source.Title: Kimya TPC-ESD 3D Filament
Source.Source note: Kimya's two-page technical data sheet for its TPC-ESD filament, created and revised 13/11/2019, as a retailer (shop3duniverse.com) serves it; kimya.fr does not answer. Filament properties on page 1, printed specimens' properties (printing direction XY) on page 2.
Source.Access note: Fetched 2026-10-07 by Claude Sonnet (quality round 2026-10-07, b45) from https://shop3duniverse.com/cdn/shop/t/116/assets/kimya-tpc-esd-3d-filament_en.pdf; staged by digest (ingest:witness --from, docs/audits/2026-10-07-quality-round/ingest/staged-manifest-b45.csv).

Skipped: Diameter 1,75 ± 0,1 mm: dimension, not a property
Charpy impact resistance ISO 179-1/1eA prints "No Break": no number
Note 1 and Note 2 (French): footnote and "indicative values" disclaimer, recorded in notes only

Block headed PRINT PARAMETERS AND SPECIMENS DIMENSIONS is the specimen print block (its heading says specimens); recorded as a profile because its nozzle and bed ranges read as settings, doubtful whether the maker recommends them
"Shore hardness of 91 A" in the intro: repeats the Shore Hardness row
Surface resistivity 10⁷ - 10⁹ Ohms/m² (ASTM D257): an exponent range in a unit the table does not hold; left in the record tier.

The block "PRINT PARAMETERS AND SPECIMENS DIMENSIONS" (nozzle 230-270 °C, bed 60-85 °C, 20-60 mm/s, 100 % rectilinear, XY) is how the test bars were printed, not a recommendation: never a profile (m170); it is the printed bars' statement of the page 2 values.

Source.Access note: Fetched 2026-10-07 by Claude Sonnet (quality round 2026-10-07, b45) from https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0541/6638/8905/files/DREMC_PBT_GF_TDS_V1.1.pdf?v=1747390078; staged by digest (ingest:witness --from, docs/audits/2026-10-07-quality-round/ingest/staged-manifest-b45.csv).

Skipped: Chemical Properties table (acid, alkali, oil and grease, organic solvent resistance): qualitative, no number
Specimen Testing conditions (0.6mm nozzle, 300 °C, 50mm/s, 0.12mm layer, infill 100%) p. 2: recorded in the params of every mechanical value, not a recommended-settings profile
Annealing Tip: 80-100 °C for 2-3 hours: a post-process recommendation, not a recorded value
Supports advice (remove supports once cooled): text only
